CHIEF COMPLAINT
Upper respiratory infection

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Andrew is a 59-year-old male presenting with upper respiratory infection. He reports that approximately one week ago while doing yard work and landscaping, he began experiencing fatigue and shortness of breath. He attributes this to catching his first cold after not wearing masks regularly at the end of summer. He describes the shortness of breath occurring primarily with exertion, specifically when lifting and carrying heavy bags of soil. He denies shortness of breath at rest. He reports feeling a little warm but attributes this to physical exertion. He denies currently coughing up sputum but anticipates this may develop. He also reports bilateral elbow pain and bilateral knee pain/tension, which he attributes to the heavy lifting involved in landscaping. He denies nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. Patient has received both COVID vaccines.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Constitutional: Reports fatigue and feeling warm, denies fever. Respiratory: Shortness of breath with exertion, anticipatory non-productive cough. Musculoskeletal: Bilateral elbow pain and bilateral knee pain/tension. Allergic: Denies seasonal allergies. Gastrointestinal: Denies nausea, vomiting, diarrhea.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Depression
Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
Hypertension

MEDICATIONS
Lisinopril 20 mg daily
Metformin (prior dose, increased during this visit)

ALLERGIES
No drug allergies noted. Patient denies seasonal allergies.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works during the week and monitors glucose and blood pressure at work but less consistently on weekends. Recently engaged in yard work and landscaping. Wife enrolled him in barre classes for relaxation which he finds helpful. Attends social gatherings such as house parties.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Normal, no fever
Heart: Heart sounds nice and strong
Lungs: Scattered rhonchi bilaterally, clears with cough
Extremities: Some edema of lower extremities
Musculoskeletal: Pain to palpation of elbows bilaterally

RESULTS
Chest X-ray: No airspace disease, no pneumonia
Hemoglobin A1C: 8% (elevated)

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Upper Respiratory Infection/Viral Syndrome: COVID test ordered to rule out COVID. Patient expected to improve in a couple of days. Prescribed Robitussin for cough. Advised to use ibuprofen and Tylenol for fever as needed.

2. Depression: Currently well-controlled with non-pharmacological measures (barre classes). Offered medication management or psychotherapy referral. Patient declined at this time; will reassess in a few months.

3. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Hemoglobin A1C elevated at 8%; goal is 6-7%. Increased metformin to 1000 mg twice daily. Hemoglobin A1C to be rechecked in 4 months.

4. Hypertension: Well-controlled on current regimen. Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily. Lisinopril refill ordered. Lipid panel ordered.

5. Follow-up: Appointment scheduled for 4 months. Patient instructed to contact if symptoms worsen.
